ruling.recommended_action: Refund $4.47 to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the non-exempt detour segment (3.17 km × $1.4098/km); no account flag (no prior upheld route dispute).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a RydeTAXI metered ride (F8), so extra kilometres driven enter the fare directly and RD-2's metered branch applies: refund = Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × per-km rate [F8][RD-2]. One off-route segment exists: 17:37–17:50, 5.85 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.68 km, adding 3.17 km [F4][RD-1].

No traffic excuse applies. There is no recorded incident near the route in the trip window [F15], and the two speed-band records (PIE and CE, band 4) are neither on the replaced stretch nor band 1–2, so RD-4(a) fails and RD-4(b) is only corroborative [F13][F14][RD-4].

RD-3 does not exempt the segment. The rider asked for "a 7-Eleven on the way" at 17:33 without naming any place, and the driver merely said "Ok" [F9][F10]. The car then stopped at 17:41–17:45 at a point 5306 m from the pickup and 4755 m from the drop-off — a location the rider never designated [F2]. Where the rider leaves the place to the driver, the stop request does not excuse the driver's own choice of a far-away outlet; the extra km of that choice are not exempt [RD-3(a),(b)]. RD-3(c) treats the stop duration separately: the 4 min 10 s wait was billed at $1.08 on the meter, which is payable on RydeTAXI and is not refundable [F2][F6][RD-3(c)].

RD-5 does not exempt it either. The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped [F11], and the only pre-segment rider message is the unnamed 7-Eleven request [F9]; no rider message before 17:37:25 agrees to any road, area or route the driver named [RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement that he "went to the one I know" is a claim, not rider consent, and cannot establish agreement [F12][RD-5].

The refund therefore comes from the non-exempt segment only: 3.17 km × $1.4098/km = $4.469 ≈ $4.47 [F4][F8][RD-2]. The billed excess distance of $5.30 covers the whole +3.8 km and would over-refund the portion not tied to the measured segment, so it is not used [F5][F1][RD-2]. The surge was 1.0× and no unpublished add-on appears, so FARE-1 adds nothing [F7][F8][FARE-1]. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: the chat consists of a stop request and a one-word agreement, the complaint concerns fare and route, and no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears anywhere in the record [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's only pre-segment message asked for 'a 7-Eleven on the way' without naming a place, and the driver answered only 'Ok' [F9][F10]; the car stopped at 17:41–17:45 at a point 5306 m from the pickup and 4755 m from the drop-off that the rider never designated [F2]. Under RD-3(a) an unnamed stop request does not excuse the driver's choice of a far-off outlet, and under RD-5 a driver's post-trip claim of agreement [F12] is not rider consent and no rider message before 17:37:25 agreed to any driver-named route (complete, fully timestamped chat [F11]). RD-4(a) fails for lack of a qualifying incident [F15], so the extra 3.17 km of this segment is refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2][RD-3][RD-4][RD-5].
